Subject: Quantamed — post-demo technical recap & next steps

Hi Emma / Diego,

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate the context on clinical triage and the long-form note synthesis workflow. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align engineering workstreams: 

• Objective: Produce a structured post-visit summary and coding suggestions from long clinical notes (20k token average) with an interactive QA mode for care teams.
• Recommended approach (high-level):
  - Inference: mix of chat-mode endpoints for multi-turn QA and completions for templated summary generation.
  - Retrieval + relevance: embeddings index for past notes + a server-side reranker to reduce latency and token bloat.
  - Structured output: function/tool-calling style JSON for downstream systems (EHR ingest), with strict schema validation on the server.
  - Auth & deployment: Private deployment (VPC) is preferred for PHI; for POC we can start with dedicated capacity and a scoped API key.

Open technical questions we need from your side to finalize the POC plan:
1) Do you prefer chat-style JSON (messages array) or single-request completions for summary jobs? Any constraints from your EHR ingestion on field ordering/optional fields?
2) Token budget: sample max_tokens we should plan for — do you expect prompts + context to exceed 25k tokens?
3) Embeddings: are you standardizing on 1536-d vectors or would you like higher-dimension vectors for clinical signal?
4) Reranker latency requirement — sub-200ms per doc is ideal for interactive flows; acceptable tail latency?
5) Any internal policy about client-side tokenization (we recommend server-side to keep prompt control).

Next steps: I attached a draft mutual-action-plan (quantamed-mutual-action-plan.xlsx). If you can answer the set above and confirm 2–3 times for a technical deep-dive next week, we’ll have Laura scope the SDK/auth deliverable and Aditya scope embeddings/reranker tests.

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Vivek / team,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our engineering side before we lock a deep-dive:

1) SDK / Auth: does Redwood provide a server-side SDK we should embed in our backend, or do you expect us to call your REST API directly? For POC we prefer minimal infra changes — a small SDK snippet would be ideal. How do you recommend handling API key rotation and per-team scopes?

2) Chat vs completions: For the templated summary job that populates our EHR fields, we prefer deterministic outputs with strict JSON — is chat mode safe for that, or should we use completions + strict stop sequences?

3) Tokenization / max_tokens: some of our notes include embedded diagnostics and scanned text; worst-case prompt+context could approach ~30k tokens. What are practical approaches to handle that (prefix caching? chunked reranking?)

4) Embeddings & reranker: what vector sizes do you support out of the box, and do you have recommendations for on-the-fly rerankers vs batch re-ranking for recall vs latency tradeoffs?

5) Streaming & structured tool-calling: when streaming a long generated JSON back to the client, how do you recommend handling partial/invalid JSON fragments (for UI preview)?

I attached a short PRD excerpt that calls out some EHR constraints. Can Laura or Aditya propose an SDK init example + a sample request/response schema we can review?

Thanks,
Emma

Hi Emma / Diego — thanks for the PRD excerpt and clear questions. Quick answers + concrete artifacts below.

1) SDK / Auth
- We provide a lightweight server-side SDK (Node/Python) that handles retry/backoff, streaming decoding, and optional telemetry. For the POC we recommend server-side initialization with scoped API keys. Keys can be rotated via our Console or programmatically using the Admin API; you can attach role-based scope (e.g., embeddings:read, inference:generate).
- Example (Node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai' });
  // server-side only — do not embed key in browser

(Attachment: sdk_auth_snippet.txt)

2) Chat vs Completions & deterministic JSON
- For strict schema outputs we recommend chat-mode with a constrained system + response schema enforcement on the server. Use a validator (JSON Schema / pydantic) after generation to reject/fallback. Chat mode is not inherently nondeterministic if you control sampling params (temperature=0, top_p=0.0) and use function-like output constraints.
- Alternatively, completions with strong stop sequences can work, but streaming with stops is trickier — model may emit after stop in rare cases. If you need absolute determinism, combine: (a) temperature=0, (b) payload-level validation, (c) small post-processing heuristics to repair common issues (unclosed brackets).

3) Token budget & handling long notes
- For ~30k token contexts we recommend this pattern:
  a) Client-side preprocessing to extract relevant spans (clinical entities) into a condensed context.
  b) Embeddings-based retrieval over document chunks (we recommend 1536-d for deg-general but offer 3072-d as an opt-in for clinical signals).
  c) Server-side reranker to reduce to top-K chunks before final prompt.
- Prefix/KV caching: Redwood supports KV cache for repeated system/prompt prefixes which can reduce effective token usage for multi-turn sessions.

4) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Out of the box we support 1536 and 3072 dims. For clinical embeddings we often see stronger signal at 3072 but larger index size.
- For interactive flows: use a lightweight dense-scorer reranker (on GPU or CPU depending on QPS). Batch re-ranking is fine for nightly ingestion; for interactive, a hybrid approach (ANN candidate retrieval -> fast rerank on top-50) hits latency targets.

5) Streaming + structured tool-calling
- Streaming semantics: we stream tokens as they are generated. For structured JSON you have two options:
  A) Non-streaming end-to-end: wait for full generation server-side, validate, then send to client (most robust).
  B) Streaming with chunk framing: send JSON chunks with explicit markers and a final end-of-object signal. Client assembles and validates; if JSON fails, fall back to full generation.
- Stop sequences in streaming: model respects stops but streaming doesn’t guarantee the last frame contains a syntactically complete JSON — include an end delimiter ("<END_JSON>") as an extra guard.

Sample request/response (chat-style)
REQUEST (pseudo):
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are a clinical summarization assistant. Output MUST match the schema in `schema.v1.json`.' },
    { role: 'user', content: '<retrieved_chunks>\nPlease produce JSON with fields: summary, differential_diagnoses, icd10_codes (list), action_items (list).' }
  ]
  temperature: 0
  max_tokens: 6000
  stream: false

RESPONSE (valid JSON)
  { "summary": "...", "differential_diagnoses": ["..."], "icd10_codes": ["R51"], "action_items": ["Order MRI"] }

Routing / Cost\/Latency tradeoff
- You can configure routing policies by intent or model size. Example: route low-latency QA to a small L1 model (cheaper) and summary generation to an L3 model. Aditya can provide a routing JSON if you want to automate this in your infra.
(Attachment: routing_diagram.pdf)

Next steps I can own: a short SDK init + sample request/response schema (I'll drop in the Drive link). Aditya will prototype an embeddings+reranker flow and return latency numbers for top-50 rerank. Vivek will coordinate the SRE schedule.

Thanks — Laura

Emma / Diego — great questions. Quick replies and proposed next steps: 

• Chunking guidance: Start with 1k–1.5k token chunks with ~200 token overlap; Aditya will run a sweep on recall for your sample set and report back.
• KV cache: Redwood’s prefix KV cache is cluster-shared in Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted the cache is per-tenant but still shared across worker processes. We’ll include explicit cache behavior in the SRE runbook.

Proposed technical deep-dive slots (PT):

  • Thu Feb 4, 09:00–10:00 PT
